description: Population, land area, GDP and CO₂ emissions of every country from the World Bank, and the first significant digit of each value. Statistics idea: Benford's law. Quantities that grow multiplicatively and span several orders of magnitude start with 1 about 30% of the time and with 9 under 5% (share log10(1 + 1/d)); a chi-square test with 8 degrees of freedom and the mean absolute deviation (MAD) say how close each quantity comes. Caveats: about 215 countries per quantity is a small sample for a digit test, values are each country's latest year, and conformity is not proof that numbers are honest (nor nonconformity proof of fraud).
name: Benford's law in country statistics
